title: My Hobby MMO
author: SquizzOC
selftext: So this still need a number of art passes, but this is my expect into creating an MMO and it’s starting to look like a game.

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body:
I’ve had three agents running for two days doing pass after pass to create the rule set for all other zones. Once I get the frame work in place, I’ll go through and audit every texture and asset to get it to the exact art style I’m aiming for which is more in line with this.

replies.author: SquizzOC

replies.author: tothjm
replies.body: Do you have to run this all locally to do mcp and use unreal, and blender or how does that connection work..also is blender free in this format

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body: Blender is completely free and yes needs to be on a machine, either on your own home machine or through a paid service like VAGON, which allows you to spin up virtual machines to do the processing for you. I used this service when I have a lot of stuff to do at once and an excess of usage left. So it’s rare, but that takes my 3 instances of Unreal up to 6

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body:
So unreal, I believe Godot has an MCP server,blender can all run locally, just ask Claude to connect to their MCP server and say “I’m new to this, give me step one, I will compete the task, say done and then you give me the next step” it’ll walk you through till you get more comfortable connecting the dots.  

For Tripo, same concept, say you want to connect and ask for the steps.  

Elevenlabs.io does some pretty great work for background sounds, music, sound effects, but if this ever went anywhere for me, I’d bring in real people to do the fine tuning and final touches. Nothing will beat that at least today.

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body:
I’d suggest watching a number of YouTube videos to get started and just asking Claude how to get started?  

I spent three weeks having ChatGPT ask me 20-59 questions a day to build out a game treatment, then took a modified task manager dashboard and had Claude build out over 1,000 tasks to get started.  

Once that was done I built tools to automate the process, the review process and just work for me 24x7.  

Best place to start is to ask Claude how to get started

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body: Thanks, the systems to me are easy to build out, the Netcode will not, but if the game doesn’t look like a world I want to explore, then it’s all pointless. So I need to prove I can get the exact art style done, then systems, then netcode for the hosted server set up

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body:
Follow me on Reddit, if I get to a state that is truly playable, I’ll build a subdomain on the games main domain to follow development.  

I’ve been at a work event for my day job all week, so most of this has been done remotely through a dashboard I built that connects the three Claude agents (all max plan and assigned to partners that will be stepping in to help when I get back to follow Claude’s ToS), Two ChatGPT and one Gemini. Gemini is worthless. I access the dash from a laptop or my phone to make sure tasks never stop.  

Once home will go through the main playable space and focus on making it match the concept art perfectly, if I can get that done, I’ll keep going and start posting

replies.author: SquizzOC
replies.body:
Thanks, I actually scrapped it all this morning. So I've been traveling for work the last 9 days and built all that from my phone through an AI Harness I built out, allowed me to use Claude to build tasks, answer questions, review results, etc... Only one system crash that my wife was able to fix by rebooting my machine and it was only due to modifying the Dashboard remotely.  

That said, I learned a lot about the limitations of just trusting Ai.  
When you say "Match the concept art exactly", well it did, but stacking assets in the background vertically with no real landscape behind it. The Image looked great, but it wasn't playable.  

So I'm using/used Gaea to build the landscape and now I'm rebuilding the town square and surrounding zone.  

So a valuable learning lesson, expensive learning lesson since it was a week of usage across 5 accounts, but lesson learned and now I can create something better.
